title: Review converging requirement and function responsibilities
goal: Determine which declared architectural allocations agree, conflict, or still require review.
context: An architect reviews requirement responsibility alongside the Functions intended to realize it.
trigger: An allocation review is needed before relying on the proposed architecture.
preconditions: A selected model state and its declared allocation rules are identifiable.

interaction.action: Selects the requirements and Functions whose architectural responsibilities need review.
Presents their declared Module responsibilities, applicable constraint paths, and allocation rules.
Identifies missing responsibilities, rule-based conflicts, declared deferrals, and questions needing engineering review.
Inspects each finding and its basis before making an architectural judgment.

expected_outcome: The architect can distinguish established allocation findings from incomplete modeling and unresolved engineering judgment.

alternatives.condition: Some Functions are deliberately unallocated under a permitted draft rule.
alternatives.outcome: The system exposes the reason and deferred scope without inventing Module ownership.

alternatives.condition: Different Modules carry related responsibilities and no rule forbids that arrangement.
alternatives.outcome: The system presents the difference for review without asserting a mechanical conflict.

alternatives.condition: The model contains no architectural allocation yet.
alternatives.outcome: The system reports the unassessed scope so the architect knows allocation consistency has not been established.

alternatives.condition: A declared allocation violates an explicit consistency rule.
alternatives.outcome: The system identifies the conflicting entities, paths, and rule so the architect can distinguish the established violation from matters requiring judgment.

failures.outcome: The system identifies the broken path and limits the assessment.

sources.basis: IR-002 analysis establishes this stakeholder situation and its selected profile boundaries; the linked SRs account for its outcomes without creating a second requirement parent. Accepted as current requirement-analysis knowledge after independent coverage and clarity review: one owning IR and primary Feature, observable goal and interactions, classified outcomes, and applicable SR coverage. This confirms analysis only, not requirement approval, implementation, or satisfaction.
